metaDescription: Spot billing traps in walkthrough questions for cleaning vendors: prevent vague scope exclusions, $15–$30 restroom add-ons, and run our Quote Comparator.
excerpt: Most janitorial contract disputes trace directly back to verbal promises and unchallenged assumptions made during the initial 30-minute site walkthrough. Discover the six costly mistakes and billing traps facility teams miss when interviewing cleaning estimators on site.
quickAnswer: The biggest mistakes facility managers make during janitorial site walkthroughs include accepting verbal assurances ('our crew takes care of all that') without written Exhibit A frequency commitments, handing estimators inflated gross Rentable Square Footage (RSF) lease sheets, and failing to lock down consumable liner and tissue markups ($0.012–$0.025/sq ft/visit). Eliminating these walkthrough blind spots prevents 25% to 45% post-contract billing creep on breakrooms ($12–$25/visit), interior glass ($15–$35/visit), and 5th-week calendar charges.

blocks.text: A commercial cleaning salesperson's primary goal during a site walkthrough is to build rapport, agree with every complaint you have about your current cleaner, and keep contractual scope definitions flexible enough to protect their gross margin. When facility teams treat the walkthrough as a casual meet-and-greet rather than an evidentiary procurement interview, they fall prey to predictable billing traps and mistakes on walkthrough questions for cleaning vendors that inflate monthly invoices within 60 days of contract launch.
1. Mistake #1: Relying on Verbal Promises That Disappear Behind 'Entire Agreement' Clauses

During the walkthrough, you point to the breakroom refrigerators, the glass conference walls, and the high HVAC supply vents. You ask, 'Will your crew handle those?' The salesperson smiles and replies, 'Absolutely, our team takes care of everything in the suite.' Two months later, the conference glass is covered in smudges and the breakroom microwave hasn't been touched. When you call the account manager, they point to the contract's merger (or 'Entire Agreement') clause—which legally voids every verbal statement made during the walkthrough—and send you a change-order quote for $25 per visit for breakroom appliance detailing and $30 per visit for interior partition glass.

blocks.title: The Merger Clause Rule in Janitorial Contracts
blocks.text: Every standard building service contractor agreement contains a boilerplate Merger Clause stating that the signed document supersedes all prior oral discussions or walkthrough notes. If an estimator says a task is included during your site tour—whether it is $12–$25/visit breakroom sanitation, $15–$35/visit interior glass, or high dusting above 72 inches—it does not exist unless it is typed into Exhibit A with an explicit daily, weekly, or monthly frequency.
2. Mistake #2: Handing Vendors Your Lease's Rentable Square Footage (RSF)

When an estimator asks, 'How many square feet is the space?' facility managers routinely quote the square footage listed on the first page of their commercial lease. In multi-tenant Class A and Class B office buildings, leases state Rentable Square Footage (RSF), which includes a 12% to 20% BOMA common-area load factor covering the building's main lobby, elevator shafts, stairwells, and mechanical corridors that the landlord's base-building crew already cleans.

If your lease states 18,000 RSF with a 16% load factor, your actual cleanable Usable Square Footage (USF) inside your suite doors is only 15,517 sq ft—and deducting locked IT server rooms and dense file storage may bring actual cleanable floor area down to 14,500 sq ft. Quoting 18,000 sq ft during the walkthrough at a benchmark rate of $0.09/sq ft/visit (10,000–24,999 sq ft bracket, 5x/week = 21.65 visits/mo) causes you to overpay by $682 every single month ($8,184 per year) for 3,500 square feet of air and landlord corridors.

blocks.text: 4. Mistake #3: Letting the Vendor Dictate Can Liner Gauges and Paper Roll Specs

One of the craftiest walkthrough billing traps happens when you open the janitor closet and ask the vendor to 'just include paper and trash bags in the quote.' When a janitorial contractor controls consumable specs without SKU-level requirements, two things happen: they mark up the invoice to the top of the $0.012 to $0.025/sq ft/visit range, or they substitute flimsy, undersized bags that split open in your breakroom and low-footage bath tissue rolls that run empty by 2:00 PM.

items: Separate Deskside Liners from Heavy Breakroom Liners: Never let a vendor bill heavy-duty liner prices for dry paper wastebaskets—or use thin deskside bags in wet breakroom bins. Stock Boardwalk 24x33 Low-Cost Office Deskside Trash Can Liners (1000-Case) with 8-micron high-density construction on coreless rolls for 12-to-16-quart desk bins, and pair them with Genuine Joe 33x39 Heavy-Duty 33-Gallon Can Liners (100-Case) built from 1.5-mil puncture-resistant resin in a flat-pack box for sharp breakroom packaging and copy-room debris.

Lock In High-Footage Jumbo Bath Tissue Specs: Prevent daily restroom run-outs and vendor restocking surcharges by supplying Scott Essential Jumbo Roll Toilet Paper 2-Ply (12-Case), delivering 1,000 feet per 2-ply roll (12,000 feet per case) on a standard 3.25-inch core, and requiring the crew to replenish dispensers as part of base restroom sanitation ($15–$30/restroom/visit).

blocks.text: 5. Mistake #4: Only Interviewing the Commissioned Sales Representative

In larger regional and national janitorial companies, the polished Business Development Manager walking your suite will never set foot in your building again once the ink dries on the contract. If you do not insist that the actual Operations Manager or Roving Area Supervisor attend the finalist walkthrough, the operational nuances you discussed—which executive office requires special wood-floor care (1.08x multiplier), which alarm keypad disarms the warehouse zone, or where biohazard step-on bins are located—get lost in a one-paragraph CRM handoff note.

items.name: Provide a Verified USF Floor Plan Before the Tour Starts
items.text: Hand every estimator a printed floor plan showing exact cleanable Usable Square Footage broken down by flooring type (carpet 1.0x, VCT/LVT 1.04x, hardwood 1.08x, ceramic tile 1.12x, polished concrete 0.95x) so nobody bids off lease RSF.

items.name: Convert Every Verbal 'Yes' into a Line Item on Your Walkthrough Sign-Off Sheet
items.text: Carry a two-page Scope Verification Checklist during the tour. When the estimator agrees that breakroom microwaves, refrigerator handles, interior conference glass, and holiday make-up cleans are included, have them initial that box before leaving.

items.name: Mandate Operations Supervisor Attendance Before Award
items.text: Require the top finalist to bring their night operations supervisor for a 15-minute pre-start walkthrough to confirm janitor closet OSHA SDS compliance, alarm codes, and waste-pull routes.

faqs.q: How should federal holidays be handled in a 5x/week (21.65 visits/month) janitorial quote?
faqs.a: Ask during the walkthrough whether the vendor deducts observed federal holidays when calculating their annualized 4.33-week monthly rate, provides a weekend make-up deep-cleaning shift for each holiday skipped, or issues a pro-rata invoice credit equal to 1/21.65th of the monthly fee whenever your office is closed on a weekday holiday.

faqs.q: What is a red flag when an estimator inspects our janitor closet during the walkthrough?
faqs.a: If an estimator barely glances inside your janitor closet without checking mop sink drainage, hot-water tap pressure, electrical outlet locations for charging floor equipment, or storage shelf space for an OSHA Safety Data Sheet (SDS) binder and secondary-labeled bottles, they are not planning a serious operational setup.

faqs.q: Why should we avoid group walkthroughs with multiple cleaning vendors at the same time?
faqs.a: In a group walkthrough, experienced estimators withhold proprietary labor-saving insights so competitors don't overhear them, while low-ball bidders stay silent and simply underbid the group atmosphere. Separate 30-minute walkthroughs let you grill each estimator on their exact ISSA production rate (3,500 sq ft/hr benchmark) and W-2 wage structure ($35–$65/hr).

faqs.q: Can a cleaning vendor charge a fuel surcharge or environmental fee that wasn't mentioned on the walkthrough?
faqs.a: Only if you fail to strike the 'ancillary fees and fuel adjustment' boilerplate from their standard service agreement. During the walkthrough, state clearly that your company only accepts a single all-inclusive monthly flat fee with zero fuel, dispatch, environmental, or administrative surcharges.
